strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#68487 in pandas at buggy commit d34d3e05636e: nanmedian with skipna=False returns bare np.nan and the 2-D apply_along_axis path casts later complex columns to float64; _get_counts_nanvar with ddof>=count widens float32 nansem/nanvar results to float64 in the 1-D path. Success is the transition: developer tests fail on buggy and pass on fixed revision.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)

python-dateutil: unbounded in evidence, unpinned by choice

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/test_nanops.py -k "nanmedian_skipna_false_keeps_dtype or nanvar_family_keeps_dtype" -p no:cacheprovider && python -m pytest pandas/tests/frame/test_reductions.py -k test_median_skipna_false_keeps_complex && python -m pytest pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_reductions.py -k test_frame_nan_result_dtype_matches_dense
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision d34d3e05636e, test_median_skipna_false_keeps_complex fails for na_first=False and/or True because df.median(skipna=False) returns a real/float64 NaN or 2.0 instead of complex values in the expected Series; test_nanmedian_skipna_false_keeps_dtype fails on the 2-D result dtype check for dtype values; test_nanvar_family_keeps_dtype fails for float16/float32 where the 1-D result dtype is widened to float64. On the fixed revision all these tests pass, so the transition is fail-to-pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1 + 2j, np.nan], "b": [1 + 2j, 3 + 4j]}); df.median(skipna=False)["b"] compared against df[["b","a"]].median(skipna=False)["b"]
risks: Behaviour depends on column order: the bug shows only when the NaN-holding column is reduced first, so both orders must be exercised (the test is parametrized over na_first).

The sparse test in pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_reductions.py references GH#68194 and SparseDtype paths; it may fail for reasons unrelated to GH#68487 on the buggy commit, so it should be treated as supplementary.
Expected NaN for complex must be complex(np.nan), not real NaN; comparison is sensitive to this.

numpy version is unbounded in evidence (no documented constraint, no era table entry); the chosen numpy release may alter apply_along_axis or scalar promotion behaviour, so the bug may not reproduce on a numpy version different from the era in which it was observed.
bottleneck is disabled via the disable_bottleneck fixture in test_nanops.py; if bottleneck is installed and the fixture is absent, the code path differs.

The defect is a dtype-promotion bug, not architecture-specific per the evidence, but float16 and complex64 behaviour may vary across platforms; no platform or sanitizer requirement is stated in the evidence.
PR date is blank in the context, so the era of the dependency set cannot be bounded from the evidence.
Editable build requires a working C compiler; build failure on the buggy revision would prevent any transition being observed.
fixed-revision commit hash is not given; the fixed revision must be taken from PR#68487 merge state.

oracle.reference_source: pandas/tests/frame/test_reductions.py test_median_skipna_false_keeps_complex; reordered column result is the reference per PR#68487 reproducer
oracle.why: Median of complex column [1+2j, 3+4j] is 2+3j exactly; dtype equality checks are exact.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On d34d3e05636e the 2-D median path casts the later complex column to float64, so the result 2.0 disagrees with expected 2+3j in tm.assert_series_equal, and the dtype assertions in the nanops tests see float64 instead of the input dtype, so these tests fail.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision missing values carry the input dtype, the complex median of column b is preserved as 2+3j, and float32/float16 nanvar/nansem results keep their dtype in both 1-D and 2-D paths, so all listed tests pass.
